messages:
ben-support: Hey team — customer (acct: acme-orchards) says their invoice token total is ~3.2M but the dashboard "served tokens" shows ~2.1M for the same month. They sent invoice id INV-2026-04-78. Can we triage? :eyes:
ira-cust-success: Thanks Ben. Customer is pretty upset, says spike started after they enabled continuous batching and KV prefetch last week. Asked for a breakdown and credits if it's on our side.
dave-billing: I pulled invoice and line items. Billing backend shows meter 'tokens.metred' = 3,217,402. Dashboard served_tokens aggregate is 2,107,981. Need to know what was counted by metering vs served pipeline.
ben-support: Attached the customer's sample request (anonymized):
```
POST /v1/completions
{
  "model": "redwood-13b",
  "prompt": "Summarize sales notes",
  "batching": { "mode": "continuous", "max_batch_wait_ms": 12 }
}
```
They said they saw many small queries with short prefixes.
clara-eng: FYI infra-bot earlier flagged a warmup flood from their API key on 2026-04-02 14:03 UTC — lots of prefetches to populate KV prefixes. That can affect metering. I'm going to pull logs.
infra-bot: Detected: key=acct-acme-orchards spike pattern. prefetch_requests=18,432 in 1h starting 2026-04-02T14:02:12Z. Average tokens/prefetch=46.
clara-eng: Raw log extract (simplified):
```
[14:03:01] batcher: assemble batch id=9fa tokens_total=120 size=4
[14:03:01] prefetch: key=acct-acme-orchards prefix=kvcache:user:42 tokens=48 result=miss
[14:03:01] serve: response tokens=6
[14:03:01] metering: billed_tokens_increment=48
```
Note the metering increment equals the prefetch tokens, not the short served response tokens.
ben-support: So our billing counted the prefetch tokens even though the user saw small final responses? That explains the gap.
dave-billing: Correct. Metering hooks run inside the serving runtime at token generation time. Prefetches are actual model calls that generate tokens (used to warm KV cache/prefixes) and are currently billable. The dashboard "served_tokens" metric is computed from the request traces that are user-facing completions and excludes internal warmups by default.
ira-cust-success: Customer says the prefetches were triggered by their "prefetch_on_write" feature in their client. They didn't realize that warmup calls are charged separately. They want guidance and a one-off credit.
clara-eng: Actionable notes: we should (1) surface internal prefetch counts in the console per API key, (2) consider tagging prefetch calls as "system_preflight" so the dashboard can show them, (3) update docs to clarify continuous batching + KV prefetch billing.
dave-billing: For this invoice I recommend a manual credit for the warmup window. I'll prepare a credit of ~1.05M tokens equivalent (matches the prefetch batch count * avg tokens). Need sign-off from ops.
ben-support: I'll draft a reply to the customer explaining the mismatch and offer the credit. Clara — can you confirm whether we can add a temporary per-key breakdown export?
clara-eng: Yes we can export logs for that key: I have a query ready:
```
select timestamp, event_type, tokens_generated, request_id
from runtime_events
where api_key = 'acct-acme-orchards' and event_type in ('prefetch','completion')
and timestamp >= '2026-04-02T13:50:00Z' and timestamp < '2026-04-02T15:00:00Z'
order by timestamp
```
I ran it and attached CSV to the ticket.
dave-billing: Got the CSV. Reconcile script shows: prefetch_total_tokens=1,105,421; completion_total_tokens=1,002,081; other=1,109,900 (other here = embeddings + rerank calls). That adds up to invoice total.
ira-cust-success: Customer wants better guardrails or a flag to disable prefetch billing. Is there a runtime switch?
clara-eng: We can add a client-side flag to avoid prefetch or switch prefetch to low-priority spot that batches with user queries; but currently prefetches are real model invocations. Workaround: set batching.max_batch_wait_ms higher or disable prefetch.
ben-support: I'll propose the credit and include steps to reduce future unexpected charges.
dave-billing: I'll issue credit after approval from ops. Tagging ops@redwood for sign-off.
ben-support: Thanks all. I'll update the support ticket and cc the customer. Keeping thread open for ops sign-off. :white_check_mark:
